standard.title: Tout / Toute / Tous / Toutes (All / Every)
standard.explanation: The word 'tout' (all, every) agrees with the noun in gender and number. Use: tout (masculine singular) / toute (feminine singular) / tous (masculine plural) / toutes (feminine plural). It is placed before the article and noun: 'tout le livre' (all the book), 'toute la page' (the whole page), 'tous les romans' (all the novels), 'toutes les histoires' (all the stories). The expression 'tout le monde' (everyone) is invariable and always singular. When used as an adverb, 'tout' means 'completely' or 'entirely' and does not change: 'tout seul' (all alone), 'tout petit' (very small).

drills.explanation: 'les personnes' is feminine plural, but we use 'tous' for plural when the context is mixed or for people in general. Actually, the correct form is 'Toutes' here since 'personnes' is feminine plural.

drills.explanation: 'la page' is feminine singular, so we use 'toute' as an adverb modifying the verb 'lis' with the meaning 'read the entire page'.

advanced.title: Tout / Toute / Tous / Toutes — Agreement, Adverb Use & Fixed Expressions
advanced.explanation: The word 'tout' agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies: tout (masc. sing.) / toute (fem. sing.) / tous (masc. pl.) / toutes (fem. pl.). When placed before an article and noun, it means 'all' or 'the whole': 'tout le livre' / 'toute la page' / 'tous les romans' / 'toutes les histoires'. As an adverb (before an adjective), 'tout' is invariable before words starting with a consonant: 'tout seul' (all alone), 'tout petit' (very small). However, before adjectives starting with a vowel or feminine adjectives, the adverbial 'tout' can agree for pronunciation: 'toute seule' (f. sg.), 'tous seuls' (m. pl.), 'toutes seules' (f. pl.). Key expressions: 'tout le monde' (everyone, invariable), 'toutes les deux' / 'tous les deux' (both, the two of them), 'tout à fait' (completely, exactly), 'tout de suite' (right away), 'tout à l'heure' (in a moment / earlier), 'en tout cas' (in any case). Note: 'tous' (plural) is pronounced with a silent 's' except when used as a pronoun ('tous' = all of them, pronounced with 'z' sound).

standard.scenario: You meet a friend at a bookstore. Recommend a book to them. Describe what the book is about and use 'tout', 'toute', 'tous', or 'toutes' at least once in your recommendation. You have 60 seconds to prepare and 90 seconds to speak.
standard.modelAnswer: Je te recommande le roman 'Le Petit Prince'. C'est l'histoire d'un jeune prince qui voyage dans l'espace. Tous les personnages sont fascinants et l'histoire est très émouvante. Toute l'aventure est magnifique. Je suis sûr(e) que tu vas aimer ce livre!
standard.modelAnswerExplanation: This response uses 'tous' (all the characters) and 'toute' (all the adventure) correctly, and provides a clear recommendation with description.
standard.tip: Remember to use complete sentences and speak clearly. Try to describe the main characters or plot before giving your opinion.

advanced.scenario: You are at a literary discussion group. Recommend a book you have recently read. Provide detailed information about the author, the characters, and themes. Use expressions like 'tous les personnages', 'tout à fait', 'toutes les pages', and 'le chapitre' in your discussion. You have 60 seconds to prepare and 120 seconds to speak.
keyPhrases: Toutes les pages sont remplies de...
advanced.modelAnswer: Je veux partager mon expérience avec le roman 'Les Misérables'. L'auteur est Victor Hugo, un des plus grands écrivains français. Tous les personnages du roman sont profonds et mémorables. Tout à fait, ce livre est un chef-d'œuvre littéraire. Le chapitre sur Jean Valjean m'a vraiment impressionné(e). Toutes les pages sont remplies de compassion et d'humanité. C'est un roman que je recommande vivement à tous les amateurs de littérature.
advanced.modelAnswerExplanation: This response demonstrates advanced usage: 'tous les personnages' (all the characters), 'tout à fait' (absolutely), 'le chapitre' (specific chapter reference), 'toutes les pages' (all the pages), and provides a sophisticated literary discussion.
advanced.tip: Use specific chapter or character references to show you have read the book. Incorporate adjectives that express your opinion (mémorable, émouvant, magnifique) and use 'tout' forms naturally in context.
